overview: Leishmaniasis is caused by a protozoa parasite from over 20 Leishmania species, with three main forms of the disease: Visceral leishmaniasis, Cutaneous leishmaniasis, and Mucocutaneous leishmaniasis. If left untreated, Visceral leishmaniasis is fatal in over 95% of cases. Leishmaniasis has outbreak and mortality potential, with an estimated 50 000 to 90 000 new cases of Visceral leishmaniasis occurring worldwide annually.
symptoms: enlargement of the spleen and liver
treatment: medicines that require an immunocompetent system
transmission: bites of infected female phlebotomine sandflies
sandflies feeding on blood to produce eggs
70 animal species, including humans, as the source of Leishmania parasites
prevention: proper housing and domestic sanitary conditions
reduced sandfly breeding and resting sites
avoiding sleeping outside or on the ground
risk_factors: poor housing and domestic sanitary conditions
